questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follows the given statements.

**Statements :**

I. No red is black.

II. No rat is black.

**Conclusions :**

I. Some rat are not red.

II. Some red are black.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d12efad2ccd61249fa399d631ba499afea0ddc1b576eb2059b229d69d1d313a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some rat are not red → Does not follow (As no red is black and no rat is black. As no direct relation is given between red and rat, therefore it is false.)

II. Some red are black → Does not follow (As no red is black. As red cannot be black, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1"

questions.question: Sri Lanka is separated from India by a narrow channel of sea formed by the Palk Strait and the ________.

__
 
• Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar.
 
• It is situated between Tamil Nadu (India) and Jaffna district (Sri Lanka).
 
• The strait is named after the former governor of Madras, Robert Palk.
 
• The Palk Strait is bounded by
 
 
• Pamban Island (India)
 
• Adam's (RAM Setu) Bridge
 
• The Gulf of Mannar (Sri Lanka)

• A strait is a narrow body of water connecting two larger bodies of water, not a gulf.
 
• Famous straits include the Strait of Hormuz and Strait of Malacca, vital for international maritime routes.
 
• Straits are often strategically significant due to their location and role in global trade.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Kutch:**
 
 
• Located on the west coast of India, in the state of Gujarat, bordering the Arabian Sea.
 
• Known for its tidal energy potential and the Rann of Kutch, a salt marsh area.
 
• It plays an important role in trade, with Kandla Port being one of India’s major seaports situated along its shores.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Khambat (also known as Gulf of Cambay)**:
 
 
• Situated on the western coast of India in Gujarat, connecting to the Arabian Sea.
 
• Known for its high tidal range and strong tidal currents, making navigation difficult.
 
• Historically important for trade and commerce, with cities like Bharuch located along its shores.

questions.question: What is Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)?

options.text: It's the percentage of deposits that banks must keep in liquid form in the short term
It's the interest rate at which banks borrow from the central bank
It's the ratio of government bonds to total assets held by a bank
It's the ratio of a bank's capital to its total assets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It's the percentage of deposits that banks must keep in liquid form in the short term.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Statutory Liquidity Ratio refers to the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities** (NDTL) that it must maintain in the form of specified liquid assets
 
• The **primary purpose of SLR **is to ensure the liquidity and solvency of banks.
 
• Thereby **SLR promotes the stability of the financial system**.
 
• SLR is mandated by the central bank of a country (for example, the Reserve Bank of India in India)
 
 
• to ensure that banks have sufficient liquidity to meet customer withdrawals and other obligations.
 
 
 
• The main objective of maintaining the SLR is to ensure the solvency and financial stability of banks and to prevent them from over-lending.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Some important Banking Terms 

 
• CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)

 
 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained as cash reserves with the central bank (e.g., the Reserve Bank of India in India).
 
• **It ensures that banks have a minimum level of liquidity to safeguard customer deposits and manage liquidity risks**.
 
• A higher CRR reduces the amount of funds available for lending, while a lower CRR increases banks' ability to lend.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks in exchange for government securities.
 
• **It is used by central banks to control inflation and manage liquidity in the economy.**
 
• When the repo rate is high, borrowing becomes more expensive for banks, which can lead to higher interest rates for consumers.
